The supply voltage and specific utility substation that will be used to supply power is still being evaluated by the utility company and will be confirmed in the next study phase. Supply voltage options include 13.2 kV, 69 kV, 138 kV and 230 kV. The design presented here is aligned with the one of the two most likely outcomes of 138kV. The other most likely voltage is 69 kV. The impact of changes in supply voltage would be addressed in subsequent project phases. The current base case design includes high voltage switchgear that will receive the incoming power supply and distribute it to two main power transformers in a parallel configuration (A and B) for 2 x 50% operation. The transformers will step the utility supply voltage down to 13.8 kV for further distribution throughout the site, with their dual configuration allowing the facility to continue operation at reduced capacity should one transformer be out of service. The neutral point of the transformer secondary windings will be resistance grounded through a neutral grounding resistor that is rated to limit fault current to 20 Amps during a ground fault event. The transformers are intended to be liquid filled with an environmentally friendly, natural or synthetic based ester. The voltage rating of the outdoor switchgear and the primary voltage rating of the two main power transformers will be dependent on the selected supply voltage to the site; however, final selection of this voltage will not have a significant impact on the overall system design since the required switchgear and transformers are available in the various supply voltage options and will not affect the proposed equipment configuration. The main switchgear, power transformers, and neutral grounding resistors for the main incoming power supply are located at the outdoor substation discussed in Section 4.5. 4.4.2 HIGH VOLTAGE POWER DISTRIBUTION The two main incoming power transformers discussed in in the previous section are connected to the 13.8kV switchgear located in the electrical room of the main site building, where it is further distributed throughout the site. The switchgear is configured in a bus A and bus B arrangement, with a main incoming circuit breaker for each bus section and an interconnecting bus tie circuit breaker between the two bus sections.
